hook: Patrick Esser studied computer vision at the IWR institute of Heidelberg University, working in Björn Ommer's Computer Vision group alongside Robin Rombach. In 2020 the pair co-authored VQGAN, published as Taming Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis, which combined a convolutional vector quantized autoencoder with a transformer to generate high resolution images. The following year he co-authored High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models with Rombach, Andreas Blattmann, Dominik Lorenz and Ommer, the paper that introduced latent diffusion and became the technical basis for Stable Diffusion. Esser and several of his CompVis colleagues later worked at Stability AI before leaving in 2024 to co-found Black Forest Labs with Rombach and Blattmann, an independent lab based in Freiburg, Germany, focused on generative visual models. The new company released its FLUX family of image generation models the same year it launched.

quick_facts: Studied in Björn Ommer's Computer Vision (CompVis) group at Heidelberg University
Co-created VQGAN, published as Taming Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis (2020)
Co-authored the Latent Diffusion Models paper that underlies Stable Diffusion (2021)
Co-founded Black Forest Labs in Freiburg, Germany, in August 2024
Black Forest Labs' FLUX models are used for text to image generation

achievements.title: Co-invented VQGAN
achievements.impact: With Robin Rombach and Björn Ommer, combined a vector quantized autoencoder with a transformer to generate high resolution, semantically coherent images, extending transformer based generation beyond low resolution pixels.

achievements.title: Co-invented Latent Diffusion Models
achievements.impact: Moved diffusion based image generation into a compressed latent space, cutting computational cost and enabling the text to image synthesis that powers Stable Diffusion.

achievements.title: Co-founded Black Forest Labs
achievements.impact: Built an independent frontier lab for visual generative AI that shipped the FLUX model family within months of launch.
